title: 5.13.4 Sub-build: Step on a grid
description: A square jumps one cell at a time, on a beat. Build the step before there is a snake.

steps.title: Run it first
steps.instructions: The square moves smoothly off the screen. A snake does not move smoothly: it steps.

steps.title: Give it a beat
steps.instructions: In `setup()`, run a function every 12 frames with `every(12, () => { ... })`. Inside it, move the block exactly one cell: `x += CELL;` where `CELL` is a constant such as 20.
hints: A smaller number is a faster snake: 8 is quick, 20 is slow.
Move by a whole cell, never by 1 pixel.

steps.title: Turn at the edges
steps.instructions: When the block reaches the right edge, send it back to the left: `if (x > width - CELL) x = 0;`.
hints: Keep the position on the grid: start at a multiple of CELL.

requirements.title: It steps on a beat
requirements.description: A timer (every or after) moves the block, not draw() every frame. Help: 5.2.1 (Reading: Random numbers and timers)

requirements.title: One whole cell
requirements.description: The move changes x by a cell-sized step (a constant, or 20/24/25). Help: 5.13.3 (Worked Example: A block that walks the grid)

aiCheck.rubricTitle: What the AI read in your code
aiCheck.prompt: The student wrote a short moSHion sketch for "Sub-build: Step on a grid". The task: move a block exactly one cell on a timer created in setup(), by adding a cell-sized constant to x, and keep it on the canvas. This is a sub-build: a small isolated program whose only job is this one mechanic. Accept any names, helpers, arrow functions and ternaries. A line only in a comment or string does not count. Use short, plain notes for a 14-year-old, name their own line when something is missing, never write corrected code.

rubric.title: A beat, made once
rubric.description: every() is called in setup() (or on an event), not inside draw().

rubric.title: A whole cell
rubric.description: x changes by a cell-sized step, not by 1 or by velocity.
